hero.title: All your coding agents. One window.
hero.lede: Vibe Manager is a native macOS app for running several Claude Code and Codex sessions in parallel, without losing track of any of them. Free and open source.
pain.title: Six terminals, three repos, two agents. Which one is waiting for you?
pain.text: When you run several agents at once, the hard part isn't the code. It's knowing where each one stands, which one is stuck, and which branch it's on. Vibe Manager keeps all of that in order for you.
features.title: Built for people who always have four agents on the go
features.lede: Each session keeps its own folder, agent, terminal, notes and history. You switch between them without restarting anything.
tasks.title: Your sessions become a task list
tasks.text: To do, running, waiting, done: every session has a status, and the sidebar shows at a glance what's moving and what's waiting. Group them by project, sort them by hand, archive them without ever losing anything.
git.title: See what the agent changed, without typing git status
git.text: The inspector tracks every repo the session touches: modified, staged and conflicted files, commits ahead of upstream. Changes are tied to the agent that made them, even when two sessions share the same folder. And your session notes sit right below.
card.quit.title: Quit, they keep going
card.quit.text: Agents can keep running while the app is closed. When you reopen it, each one is on screen just as you left it.
card.reply.title: Reply without switching sessions
card.reply.text: A background session has a question? Answer it from a palette, without leaving what you're doing.
card.switch.title: Switch agents mid-task
card.switch.text: Go from Claude Code to Codex, or from one model to another. The new agent gets a summary of the work, which you review before it's sent.
card.templates.title: Prompt templates
card.templates.text: “Review {{url}}”: one form, an exact preview, and the session starts named after the MR.
card.web.title: Terminals and a web view per session
card.web.text: A terminal drawer for the server and logs, and a web view the agent can drive: open, read the console, take screenshots.
card.local.title: Everything stays on your Mac
card.local.text: No account, no telemetry. The app reads no API keys and never lowers your CLIs' permissions.
keys.title: Everything is a shortcut away
keys.p: Find a session by ticket number, MR URL, branch or a word from its notes.
keys.j: Open the session's terminal drawer, in its folder.
keys.u: See time and tokens used, by session, agent or model.
oss.title: Free, open, and built in public
oss.lede: The code is on GitHub, every architecture decision is documented there, and the roadmap is decided in the issues.
oss.adr: Published architecture decisions, from session storage to the terminal.
oss.agents: Agents supported today: Claude Code and Codex CLI.
support.title: Vibe Manager is free. A tip helps it grow.
support.lede: No paid tier, no ads, no data collected. If the app saves you time, you can support its development. Every contribution pays for time spent on your issues.
support.sponsors_text: Monthly or one-time, from $1. GitHub takes no commission.
final.title: Take back control of your agents
cl.title: What's new
cl.lede: Every Vibe Manager release, what it adds and what it fixes. Numbers link to GitHub issues.
cl.notes_language: Release notes are written in French.
contrib.title: Vibe Manager moves at the pace of your issues
contrib.lede: A bug that bugs you, a missing workflow, a half-formed idea: open an issue. Every release is built from what users write there.
contrib.bug.title: Something doesn't work
contrib.bug.text: The more precise, the faster it's fixed.
contrib.bug.l1: What you did, what you expected
contrib.idea.title: Something's missing
contrib.idea.text: Describe the situation rather than the solution.
contrib.idea.l1: What you were trying to do
contrib.code.title: You want to dig in
contrib.code.text: Swift 6, SwiftUI, and a documented architecture.
contrib.code.l1: Pick an open issue and say so in a comment
contrib.code.l2: The README explains how to build and test
contrib.any_language: Write in whatever language you like.
contrib.flow.title: What happens to your issue
contrib.flow.s1.title: It's read and triaged
contrib.flow.s1.text: Bug, improvement or question: it gets a label and, if needed, a few questions.
contrib.flow.s2.title: It's designed in public
contrib.flow.s2.text: The design proposal is written as a comment on the issue, before a single line of code.
contrib.flow.s3.title: It ships in a release
contrib.flow.s3.text: The pull request references the issue, and the changelog mentions it on release.

support.liberapay_text: By card, SEPA direct debit or PayPal. A French non-profit that takes no commission.
perso.title: Describe it, an agent makes it
perso.lede: The avatar that alerts you and the theme of your conversations each take one sentence. The app checks every result before keeping it, and everything can be exported.
avatar.title: An avatar that gives you a wave
avatar.text: When a session is waiting for your answer and you're in another app, your avatar pops up on top with the question. You reply without going back to Vibe Manager. Codex draws it with its ten expressions in about a minute, or you import your own.
avatar.prompt: A small red fox in a navy blue hoodie, soft 3D illustration style, big expressive eyes, looking curious and friendly.
theme.title: A theme that suits you
theme.text: Six themes come built in. For your own, describe the mood: Claude Code or Codex picks the colors, the fonts and even the background picture. Each version applies live, contrast is checked so everything stays readable, and you can export it.
theme.prompt_dark: A dark forest-at-night theme: deep greens, an amber accent, and a misty forest at dusk in the background.
theme.prompt_light: Japanese paper: cream background, black ink, a touch of vermilion, a serif font and ink-wash mountains in the background.
